expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: No. The fix you shipped is a detection-rung device dressed as a control, and it has holes of its own.

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: It's a read-then-write race. Two workers picking up the same message... both see 'no recent charge' and both charge.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: Make the key a required parameter on your Stripe wrapper — not optional-for-backward-compat. Idempotency key derived from the intent, passed on every Stripe POST.

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: DB UNIQUE (idempotency_key) on your payments table, inserted before the Stripe call (pending), updated after

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Defect: 340 customers charged twice. Mistake: the redelivered message called charge() again. Hazard: a charge can be created without an idempotency key.

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: at-least-once delivery guarantees this will happen again. That's the system property.

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: Grep every Stripe POST and every consumer of that queue. Anything else that calls Stripe — refunds, subscription changes, a backfill script — is still unguarded.

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: The first incident was probably a different consumer with the same shape — that's what 'second time' usually means. Recommends Control-rung idempotency key device.

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Stripe has supported Idempotency-Key; your code lets a charge exist without one. Frames as system design, not human error.
